speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: asked	the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) since its inception, what is the respective amount of funds that have been disbursed from the Cultural Matching Fund to (i) national companies and museums (ii) major grant and seed grant companies, (iii) other cultural and arts organisations not covered in (i) and (ii); (b) what is the number of receiving entities within each of these categories; and (c) what is the amount that has been respectively disbursed to the (i) visual arts, (ii) performing arts, (iii) literary arts, (iv) traditional arts and (v) heritage sectors.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Looking at it, out of $200 million, $152 million has been actually used up.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: So, would this scheme stop when the current Cultural Matching Fund runs out?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Would the Government continue to support this scheme?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The second supplementary question is: under what conditions are applications for such Cultural Matching grants rejected?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly, I do note that a huge sum has gone to the national companies.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: So, I am wondering, while this Fund is good for companies, but at the same time, I think the rationale behind it is to help to build other companies in terms of their capacity to get sponsorship.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Has this aim been achieved and how do you ensure that this process is being cultivated?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As for the eligibility for the CMF matching, in order to qualify for CMF, applications must meet the following criteria.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But CMF may also consider other charities and IPCs that contribute significantly to the arts and heritage sectors.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: CMF will also match donations with benefits that are in line with the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore guidelines on donations with benefits.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In terms of calculation of the amount of cash donations, it is based on the amount that is received up to the previous financial year of the receiving organisation.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, applications which do not meet these above criteria will be rejected.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: On the Member's questions about the inclusion of national companies and museums, CMF's primary objective is to promote cultural philanthropy and to encourage individuals and corporations to include arts and heritage causes in their giving.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: National companies and museums, being larger organisations, are able to raise funds on a bigger scale and will have a greater impact to move the needle in raising public awareness of and support for cultural philanthropy.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This cap limits the amount of funding that each CMF recipient can obtain, and this will ensure that smaller groups can still tap on CMF over the longer term.
